question: From October 1, 2023, which organisation has introduced the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is European Union.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (कार्बन सीमा समायोजन तंत्र) is a carbon tariff introduced by the European Union (EU) on imports of carbon-intensive goods.

• Its transitional phase began on 1 October 2023, with the definitive regime starting in 2026.

• CBAM aims to prevent 'carbon leakage' and put a fair price on the carbon emitted during the production of goods like cement, iron, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen entering the EU.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• CBAM is a key part of the EU's 'Fit for 55' package aimed at cutting greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030.

• Importers must report the embedded emissions in their goods and eventually buy CBAM certificates.

• India, a large exporter of steel and aluminium to the EU, has raised concerns about CBAM at the WTO.

NOTE

• United Nations (Option 1): The global inter-governmental organisation founded in 1945 for international peace and security; it does not levy carbon tariffs.

• BRICS (Option 2): An economic grouping of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and newer members; it is not the body behind CBAM.

• International Court of Justice (Option 4): The principal judicial organ of the UN based at The Hague that settles legal disputes between states.

question: Which of the following persons is associated with the sport of shooting?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manu Bhaker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manu Bhaker (मनु भाकर) is an Indian shooter (pistol) from Haryana.

• At the Paris 2024 Olympics, she won two bronze medals (10m air pistol and 10m air pistol mixed team), becoming the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympics after independence.

• She has also won multiple gold medals at ISSF World Cups and the Commonwealth Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Shooting is one of India's most successful Olympic disciplines, with Abhinav Bindra winning India's first individual Olympic gold (10m air rifle) in 2008.

• Manu Bhaker was chosen as India's flag-bearer (along with P.R. Sreejesh) at the Paris 2024 closing ceremony.

NOTE

• D Gukesh (Option 1): Indian chess Grandmaster who became the youngest ever World Chess Champion in 2024.

• Mithali Raj (Option 3): Former captain of the Indian women's cricket team and a legendary batter.

• Dipa Karmakar (Option 4): Indian artistic gymnast famous for performing the Produnova vault at the Rio 2016 Olympics.

question: Who was appointed as the Governor of Manipur in December 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajay Kumar Bhalla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ajay Kumar Bhalla (अजय कुमार भल्ला) was appointed as the Governor of Manipur in December 2024.

• He is a retired 1984-batch IAS officer who earlier served as the Union Home Secretary for an extended tenure.

• He took charge as Governor amid the ongoing ethnic situation in Manipur (राज्यपाल).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a State, appointed by the President under Article 155 of the Constitution.

• Ajay Kumar Bhalla succeeded Anusuiya Uikey as Governor of Manipur.

NOTE

• Anusuiya Uikey (Option 2): The previous Governor of Manipur, who was earlier Governor of Chhattisgarh.

• V.K. Singh (Option 3): Former Army Chief and Union Minister who was appointed Governor of Mizoram in 2024.

• Lakshman Prasad Acharya (Option 4): Governor of Sikkim (and given additional charge of Manipur at one point).

question: In December 2024, who has been appointed as the Managing Director of SBI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rama Mohan Rao Amara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rama Mohan Rao Amara (राम मोहन राव अमारा) was appointed as a Managing Director of the State Bank of India (SBI) in December 2024.

• The appointment was made by the government on the recommendation of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB).

• SBI is India's largest public sector bank, headquartered in Mumbai (भारतीय स्टेट बैंक).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SBI is chaired by a Chairman and has several Managing Directors overseeing different verticals.

• Rama Mohan Rao Amara earlier headed SBI Cards and Payment Services as MD & CEO.

NOTE

• Paramesh Sivamani (Option 1): A senior officer who was appointed Director General of the Indian Coast Guard.

• Kais Saied (Option 3): The President of Tunisia, unrelated to Indian banking.

• Abhyuday Jindal (Option 4): An Indian industrialist, Managing Director of Jindal Stainless Ltd.

question: In August 2024, who has been appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parvathaneni Harish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Parvathaneni Harish (पर्वतनेनी हरीश) was appointed as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in August 2024.

• He is a senior Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer of the 1990 batch.

• He succeeded Ruchira Kamboj, India's first woman Permanent Representative to the UN (संयुक्त राष्ट्र में भारत के स्थायी प्रतिनिधि).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Permanent Representative heads India's Permanent Mission to the UN in New York and represents India in the General Assembly and Security Council.

• India served as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the 2021-22 term.

NOTE

• Tejpaul Bhatia (Option 1): An Indian-origin businessman/technologist appointed as CEO of Cricket USA (USA Cricket).

• Santosh Kumar (Option 2): A common name; not associated with this appointment.

• Ajay Bhushan Pandey (Option 3): A retired IAS officer who became Chairperson of the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA).

question: Under Subhadra Yojana introduced in September 2024 by Odisha government, over what period (in years) do beneficiaries receive Rs. 50000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Subhadra Yojana (सुभद्रा योजना) was launched by the Odisha government in September 2024 for women.

• Eligible women receive a total of Rs. 50,000 over 5 years, i.e., Rs. 10,000 per year paid in two instalments of Rs. 5,000 each.

• It is Odisha's flagship women-centric welfare scheme.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 17 September 2024.

• The instalments are typically credited around Rakhi Purnima and International Women's Day, aiming to promote financial empowerment of women aged 21 to 60.

NOTE

• 3 (Option 1): Incorrect; the benefit is spread over 5 years, not 3.

• 4 (Option 3): Incorrect; not the tenure of the scheme.

• 6 (Option 4): Incorrect; the scheme runs for 5 years (Rs. 10,000 x 5 = Rs. 50,000).

question: Department of Health Research has organized _______ Campaign from 17th September 2024 to 2nd October 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swachhata Hi Seva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swachhata Hi Seva (स्वच्छता ही सेवा) campaign was organised from 17th September to 2nd October 2024.

• 'Swachhata Hi Seva' means 'Cleanliness is Service'; the 2024 theme was 'Swabhav Swachhata, Sanskaar Swachhata'.

• It is an annual fortnight-long cleanliness drive leading up to Gandhi Jayanti and the anniversary of the Swachh Bharat Mission.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014, marking Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.

• 2 October 2024 marked the 10th anniversary of the Swachh Bharat Mission.

NOTE

• Swachhata Hi Shikha (Option 2): Not a recognised government campaign name.

• Swachhata Hi Puja (Option 3): Not an official campaign under this drive.

• Swachhata Hi Vandana (Option 4): Not an actual government campaign; a distractor option.

question: The typically Judo platform is of which shape?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Square.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Judo competition mat (called a tatami) is laid out in a square (वर्ग) shape.

• The contest area, along with the safety zone around it, forms a square platform.

• Judo is a modern Japanese martial art and Olympic sport founded by Jigoro Kano.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The competition area in judo is typically a minimum of 14m x 14m including the safety area, with the contest area inside it.

• Judo became an Olympic sport for men in 1964 (Tokyo) and for women in 1992 (Barcelona).

NOTE

• Rectangular (Option 2): Shape used for playfields like basketball or tennis courts, not the judo mat.

• Hexagon (Option 3): A six-sided shape associated with the MMA 'octagon/hexagon' cage, not judo.

• Circular (Option 4): Round shape used in sports like sumo (dohyo), not the judo platform.

question: In which year did India won their first Olympic gold medal in hockey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics (एम्स्टर्डम ओलंपिक).

• The legendary Major Dhyan Chand was the star of that team, scoring prolifically.

• This began India's golden era in hockey.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India won six consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals from 1928 to 1956.

• In total, the Indian men's hockey team has won 8 Olympic gold medals, the most by any nation.

• India also won bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, ending a 41-year Olympic medal drought in hockey.

NOTE

• 1900 (Option 1): The Paris Olympics; India did not win a hockey gold then.

• 1896 (Option 2): The first modern Olympics in Athens, which did not feature field hockey.

• 1924 (Option 3): The Paris Olympics; India's hockey golden run had not yet begun.

question: Which of the following game is known as the "Gentleman's Game"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cricket (क्रिकेट) is popularly known as the 'Gentleman's Game'.

• The nickname comes from the sport's origins in England and its traditional emphasis on fair play, etiquette and 'the spirit of the game'.

• The game is governed globally by the International Cricket Council (ICC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The oldest form is Test cricket; other formats include ODIs and T20s.

• The MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club) is the custodian of the Laws of Cricket.

• India won the first-ever T20 World Cup in 2007 and the 50-over World Cup in 1983 and 2011.

NOTE

• Kabaddi (Option 1): A traditional South Asian contact team sport, not called the Gentleman's Game.

• Badminton (Option 2): A racquet sport played with a shuttlecock, an Olympic discipline.

• Lawn tennis (Option 3): A racquet sport; while genteel in origin, the 'Gentleman's Game' nickname belongs to cricket.

question: The shape of Basketball must be _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is spherical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A basketball must be spherical (गोलाकार), i.e., perfectly round in shape.

• It is an inflated ball, traditionally orange with black seams, gripped and dribbled by hand.

• Basketball is played between two teams of five players each.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.

• It is governed internationally by FIBA; the standard men's ball is size 7.

• Basketball became an Olympic sport at the 1936 Berlin Games.

NOTE

• cylindrical (Option 2): A tube-like shape (like a can), not the shape of a basketball.

• geoid (Option 3): The irregular shape of the Earth's gravitational surface, not a ball shape.

• conical (Option 4): A cone shape, which a basketball is not.

question: Major Dhyan Chand is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hockey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Major Dhyan Chand was a legendary Indian field hockey (हॉकी) player.

• Known as 'The Wizard' for his extraordinary ball control, he led India to Olympic hockey gold in 1928, 1932 and 1936.

• His birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India's highest sporting honour was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2021.

• The Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium in New Delhi is named after him.

NOTE

• Shooting (Option 1): A precision sport; associated with players like Abhinav Bindra and Manu Bhaker.

• Cricket (Option 3): The bat-and-ball game; not Dhyan Chand's sport.

• Badminton (Option 4): A racquet sport; associated with players like P.V. Sindhu and Saina Nehwal.

question: Which of the following two states have jointly conducted a Nilgiri Tahr census in April 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala and Tamil Nadu (केरल और तमिलनाडु) jointly conducted the Nilgiri Tahr census in April 2025.

• The Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius) is an endangered mountain ungulate and the State Animal of Tamil Nadu.

• It is found in the montane grasslands (shola) of the Western Ghats.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Nilgiri Tahr is listed as 'Endangered' on the IUCN Red List.

• Eravikulam National Park in Kerala hosts the largest population of the Nilgiri Tahr.

• Tamil Nadu launched a dedicated 'Project Nilgiri Tahr' for its conservation.

NOTE

• Odisha and Jharkhand (Option 1): Eastern states outside the Nilgiri Tahr's Western Ghats habitat.

• Odisha and West Bengal (Option 2): Eastern coastal states; not associated with this census.

• Maharashtra and Karnataka (Option 4): Although part of the Western Ghats, they did not conduct the Nilgiri Tahr census jointly.

question: As of July 2025, how many total Ramsar Sites does India has?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 91.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2025, India has 91 Ramsar Sites (रामसर स्थल), i.e., Wetlands of International Importance.

• India crossed 91 sites after the addition of new wetlands such as Khichan and Menar in Rajasthan in 2025.

• India has the largest network of Ramsar Sites in Asia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, and came into force in 1975.

• India became a party to the Convention in 1982.

• Tamil Nadu has the highest number of Ramsar Sites among Indian states.

NOTE

• 75 (Option 1): India crossed 75 Ramsar Sites during the 75th year of independence (Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav); it has since increased.

• 82 (Option 2): An intermediate figure, not the July 2025 total.

• 85 (Option 3): Also an earlier interim count, not the correct July 2025 total.

question: Which Indian city hosted the final match of the Women's Premier League (Cricket) 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mumbai (मुंबई) hosted the final of the Women's Premier League (WPL) 2025, played at the Brabourne Stadium.

• Mumbai Indians defeated Delhi Capitals to win the WPL 2025 title.

• The WPL is the women's franchise T20 league run by the BCCI.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The inaugural WPL was held in 2023, also won by Mumbai Indians.

• Harmanpreet Kaur captains the Mumbai Indians women's team.

• The 2025 season matches were held in Vadodara, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Mumbai.

NOTE

• Chennai (Option 2): Capital of Tamil Nadu and home to the Chepauk stadium; did not host the WPL 2025 final.

• Kolkata (Option 3): Home of Eden Gardens; not the WPL 2025 final venue.

• Vadodara (Option 4): Hosted several WPL 2025 league matches but not the final.

question: _______ U23 National Basketball Championship for Men & Women was held in Assam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1st.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1st (पहली) U23 National Basketball Championship for Men & Women was held in Assam.

• It was organised by the Basketball Federation of India (BFI) at the Sarusajai Indoor Stadium in Guwahati in 2025.

• It was the inaugural edition of this age-group national championship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Basketball in India is governed by the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), affiliated to FIBA.

• In the inaugural U23 event, Haryana and Tamil Nadu were among the champions in the men's and women's categories.

NOTE

• 2nd (Option 2): Incorrect; the Assam event was the first edition, not the second.

• 3rd (Option 3): Incorrect; there was no prior edition making this the third.

• 4th (Option 4): Incorrect; the championship was newly launched (1st edition).

question: Which folk dance of Ladakh is performed in Leh and is preceded by a horse race?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Koshan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Koshan (कोशन) is a folk dance of Ladakh performed in Leh, and it is traditionally preceded by a horse race.

• It is one of the many community and festival dances of the Ladakh region.

• Ladakh's dance forms are closely tied to Buddhist festivals and local traditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019 after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir.

• Other Ladakhi dances include Jabro, Chabs-Skyan and the masked Cham dance of monasteries.

NOTE

• Sikmari (Option 1): Another Ladakhi folk dance form, but not the one preceded by a horse race in Leh.

• Mamita (Option 3): A harvest festival and folk dance associated with Tripura, not Ladakh.

• Lezim (Option 4): A vigorous folk dance from Maharashtra performed with a lezim (a small musical instrument with jingling cymbals).

question: As of July 2025, the Power Finance Corporation holds which of the following CPSE status?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharatna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2025, Power Finance Corporation (PFC) holds Maharatna (महारत्न) status among Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).

• PFC was granted Maharatna status in October 2021, becoming the 11th Maharatna CPSE.

• PFC is a leading Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) financing India's power sector, under the Ministry of Power.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Maharatna status gives a CPSE greater financial and operational autonomy for investments.

• To qualify as a Maharatna, a company must already be a Navratna, listed with prescribed public shareholding, and meet high turnover, net worth and net profit thresholds.

• PFC's subsidiary REC Ltd is also a Maharatna.

NOTE

• Navratna (Option 2): A lower category of CPSE status with less autonomy than Maharatna; PFC was upgraded from Navratna to Maharatna.

• Miniratna-I (Option 3): A category for profit-making CPSEs with limited autonomy, below Navratna.

• Miniratna-II (Option 4): The lowest of these special CPSE categories, with the least delegated powers.

question:
Which of the following is the target of National Logistics Policy-2022?
I. To increase logistics cost.
II. To develop a data-driven decision support system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Logistics Policy (NLP) 2022 (राष्ट्रीय लॉजिस्टिक्स नीति 2022) aims to develop a data-driven decision support system (Statement II is correct).

• Statement I is wrong: the policy seeks to reduce (not increase) logistics cost in India to globally competitive levels.

• Hence only Statement II is a valid target.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NLP 2022 was launched by PM Narendra Modi in September 2022 to complement the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.

• Its 'Comprehensive Logistics Action Plan (CLAP)' includes a Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP).

• A key goal is to improve India's ranking in the Logistics Performance Index (LPI).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because increasing logistics cost is the opposite of the policy's aim (which is to reduce cost).

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, as Statement I is false.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as Statement II is a genuine target of the policy.

question: The Special Economic Zones Act, 2005, was passed by the Indian Parliament in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is May, 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act, 2005 (विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र अधिनियम, 2005) was passed by the Indian Parliament in May 2005.

• It received the President's assent in June 2005 and came into force in February 2006 along with the SEZ Rules.

• An SEZ is a duty-free enclave treated as foreign territory for trade operations, duties and tariffs to boost exports.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's SEZ policy was first introduced in the EXIM Policy in 2000.

• Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) was set up at Kandla, Gujarat, in 1965.

• SEZs offer incentives such as tax benefits and simplified procedures to attract investment.

NOTE

• July, 2005 (Option 2): Incorrect; the Act had already been passed by Parliament by May 2005.

• September, 2005 (Option 3): Incorrect; not the month of the Act's passage.

• December, 2005 (Option 4): Incorrect; the SEZ Act was passed earlier, in May 2005.

question: Among these, which state experienced a population of over 100 million as per 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the 2011 Census, Bihar (बिहार) had a population of about 104 million (10.41 crore), crossing the 100 million mark.

• Among the given options, only Bihar had over 100 million people.

• Bihar was the third most populous state in India in 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The three states with population over 100 million in Census 2011 were Uttar Pradesh (~199.8 million), Maharashtra (~112.4 million) and Bihar (~104.1 million).

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state, and Sikkim the least populous.

• The 2011 Census was the 15th national census of India.

NOTE

• West Bengal (Option 1): Its 2011 population was about 91.3 million, below 100 million.

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Its 2011 population was about 72.6 million, below 100 million.

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Its 2011 population was about 68.5 million, below 100 million.

question: In the context of public goods, what does "Non-rivalrous" stands for?
option_1: One person's use reduces another's use
option_2: One person's use doesn't reduce another's use
option_3: The good is a Giffen good
option_4: The good is only available for bureaucrats
solution_text:
The correct answer is One person's use doesn't reduce another's use.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A non-rivalrous (अप्रतिस्पर्धी) good is one where one person's consumption does not reduce its availability for others.

• This is a defining feature of public goods, which are both non-rivalrous and non-excludable.

• Example: national defence or a lighthouse — one person benefiting does not diminish the benefit to others.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Non-excludable means no one can be prevented from using the good, which leads to the 'free-rider problem'.

• Because of free-riding, private markets tend to under-provide public goods, so the government often provides them.

NOTE

• One person's use reduces another's use (Option 1): This describes a 'rivalrous' good (like food or clothing), the opposite of non-rivalrous.

• The good is a Giffen good (Option 3): A Giffen good is one whose demand rises as its price rises; unrelated to non-rivalry.

• The good is only available for bureaucrats (Option 4): Not an economic definition; a distractor with no theoretical basis.

question: In the context of wear and tear in production process, the replacement investment is same as _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is depreciation of capital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Replacement investment equals the depreciation of capital (पूंजी का मूल्यह्रास), i.e., spending to make good the wear and tear of existing capital.

• Depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) is the fall in the value of capital goods due to normal wear, tear and obsolescence.

• Replacing worn-out machines simply maintains the existing capital stock rather than adding to it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gross Investment − Depreciation = Net Investment; replacement investment covers only the depreciation portion.

• The relationship also underlies the difference between GDP and NDP: NDP = GDP − Depreciation.

NOTE

• subsidy given by government (Option 2): A financial grant/aid by the government to producers or consumers; unrelated to capital wear and tear.

• wage of total staffs (Option 3): Payment to labour, a factor income, not replacement of capital.

• entrepreneurship cost (Option 4): The reward/cost related to the entrepreneur (profit), not depreciation.

question: The term 'atman' in the Upanishads refers to _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The inner self or soul.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Upanishads, the term 'Atman' (आत्मा) refers to the inner self or soul — the true, eternal essence of an individual.

• A central teaching is the identity of Atman (individual self) with Brahman (the universal, ultimate reality).

• This idea is captured in the great sayings (Mahavakyas) like 'Tat Tvam Asi' (That Thou Art).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Upanishads are philosophical texts forming the concluding part of the Vedas, hence called Vedanta.

• There are traditionally 108 Upanishads, of which the principal ones number around 10-13.

• 'Satyameva Jayate' in India's national emblem is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.

NOTE

• Ritual fire (Option 1): Refers to 'Agni', the sacrificial fire of Vedic rituals, not Atman.

• Sacred chant (Option 2): Refers to a 'mantra', a sacred utterance, not the self/soul.

• Supreme god (Option 3): Closer to 'Ishvara/Brahman' as ultimate reality; Atman specifically means the inner self, which is realised to be one with Brahman.

question: Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maitrakas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of the Maitraka dynasty (मैत्रक वंश) of Vallabhi in Gujarat.

• The Maitrakas ruled the Saurashtra region with their capital at Vallabhi.

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited Vallabhi during Dhruvasena II's reign in the 7th century CE.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dhruvasena II (Dhruvabhata) was a contemporary and son-in-law of the great emperor Harshavardhana of Kannauj.

• Vallabhi was a renowned centre of learning, famous for its Buddhist university, comparable to Nalanda.

NOTE

• Satavahana (Option 2): An ancient dynasty of the Deccan (c. 2nd century BCE onward); notable ruler Gautamiputra Satakarni.

• Chola (Option 3): A powerful South Indian dynasty; famous rulers include Rajaraja I and Rajendra I.

• Kushan (Option 4): A Central Asian dynasty; its greatest ruler was Kanishka, a patron of Buddhism.
